0.long_answer: The procedure is a bone marrow transplant, also referred to as hematopoietic stem cell transplantation. This treatment involves the destruction of the patient's defective or diseased bone marrow by high doses of chemotherapy or radiation, followed by the infusion of healthy stem cells from a matching donor (or sometimes from the patient’s own cells, in an autologous transplant). It is commonly used to treat severe bone marrow diseases such as leukemia and other cancers because it replaces the faulty marrow with cells capable of producing healthy blood components. In the case of severe sideroblastic anemia, where the bone marrow has significant dysfunction and is unable to produce adequate and properly functioning red blood cells, a bone marrow transplant may also be considered as an option to restore normal blood cell production.
